Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 03-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - JANUARY 2026  
  Distributed Systems [CSE_3251]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                 Define a distributed system and identify its main characteristics.                                    (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)            Show the different middleware organizations? Give examples.                                           (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)            Illustrate the layered architectural design of distributed systems with examples.                     (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                 Organize the essential foundations of distributed communication.                                      (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)            Show the working of Remote Procedure Call (RPC).                                                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)            Compare and contrast message-oriented communication and multicast communication.                      (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                 Identify the components of a naming system? Explain briefly with suitable examples.                   (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)            Give the advantages and disadvantages of flat naming.                                                 (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)            Infer the use of hierarchical naming used in distributed systems?                                     (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                 Demonstrate the concept of synchronization in distributed systems.                                    (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  Page #1

B)                Illustrate the vector clocks and how they solve causal ordering.                                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                Describe the Bully election algorithm with an example.                                                (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5)                        Show replica management with suitable example.                                                        (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                            Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Identify the difference between strong and eventual consistency.                                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                Discuss consistency protocols used in large-scale AI data centres.                                    (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"
